title: Make athena drain work user-queued (ask --later) requests too
summary: Drain's queue (steward::queued_work) filters to channel "steward", while `ask --later` records channel "cli", so user-deferred requests are never worked. Make queued_work include both channels, oldest first, update its docs and tests. Audience: the user who queues requests and expects drain to work them.

defaults_applied.how: Tests for queued_work and drain with cli-channel requests; cargo test and clippy clean.
Fix the channel filter in queued_work, not individual jobs.
Criteria run tests showing a cli request is worked.
One focused change to queue selection.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Requests queued by `athena ask --later` have channel "cli" (reading.rs queue); that is the only user channel to add.
Drain's existing budget, max_jobs and retry limits keep applying to user requests.
Mixed order is by received_at then job id, as now.
The named jobs are examples; this change does not work or close them.

acceptance_criteria.text: A unit test in steward.rs shows queued_work returns unread requests from both the steward channel and the cli channel (as `ask --later` writes), oldest first, and still excludes jobs that are no longer Queued. Run `cargo test -p athena-core queued_work`.
A drain test with a cli-channel queued request in the records shows drain's QueueView lists it as an item and works it. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli drain`.

The doc comments and text that say drain takes only the steward channel and never user-deferred requests (steward.rs REQUEST_CHANNEL, drain.rs, docs/decisions.md entry near line 2206) are corrected, and a decision entry/CHANGELOG line records the change and why.
`cargo test` passes, `cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean, and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
The fix is in the shared queue selection, not a special case for the named job ids; ordering and retry rules are unchanged.

out_of_scope: Working the four named jobs themselves
Changing drain's budget, retry or rating rules
Changing how steward proposals are approved
